Class SlotFlowElement

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.slot.SlotFlowElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.PanelElement
public final class SlotFlowElement extends com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
Lays out a panel's registered slots to fit its width, the way text and elements size to fit. One PanelElement owns the panel's slots and flows the visible ones into the panel's available content width, wrapping onto new rows below.

Why a flow and not a fixed grid

With slots at fixed (childX, childY) positions on a declared column count, a panel whose groups reveal separately has to pin a wide fixed width to reserve the largest extent. That leaves empty space when only a narrow group is shown, and slides the panel sideways (a flicker) when a wider group reveals over a narrow one near the screen edge. This element has no fixed grid and no pinned width: the visible slots flow into whatever width the panel has this frame, and the panel fits around the result.

Stable budget, fitted size

naturalWidth() reports the width of all slots in one row, which doesn't depend on which groups are revealed. The panel computes contentWidth = min(naturalWidth, ceiling). The natural width is almost always larger than the screen-edge ceiling the placement layer sets, so the budget passed to layoutWithin(int) is that ceiling, which depends on screen geometry and not on slot visibility, so it stays the same across reveals. The panel therefore never re-runs its cached configuration pass when a group toggles: getWidth(), getHeight() and render(RenderContext) recompute the fitted layout from the current visibility every frame against that budget. The panel reports the fitted width, so it stays narrow and never triggers the screen-edge slide, while the flow knows it may grow up to the budget before wrapping. Reveals need no extra handling, and there is no empty space and no flicker.

Client rendering only

The flow positions are presentation only. Each child SlotElement resolves its live slot by identity and writes its Slot.x/y every frame, so the real synced slots' identity and sync are untouched; only where vanilla draws and hit-tests them changes. Its slots stay live under the panel through presentsSlotAt(InputContext). The empty cells of a partial last row belong to the panel and are inert.
